title.narrative: Protection assistance for Conflict-Affected persons in Goma and surrounding territories

description.narrative: The humanitarian situation in Goma, aggravated by fighting between the FARDC and the M23, has resulted in the displacement of 23,392 people since January 20, 2025. Attacks, sexual violence, and forced displacements plunge the populations of North into fear. Over 700,000 people have fled the fighting since the beginning of the year, many finding refuge in already overcrowded camps or with host families. This situation only exacerbates the number of cases of sexual violence that were already being recorded. This figure includes those coming not only from Goma but also from surrounding localities. The security situation in the city remains worrying due to the increase in criminal acts, including home invasions, sexual violence, thefts and assaults. Humanitarian cluster noticed that following the dismantling of displacement sites around the city, at least 3,680 households (16,560 people) who were unable to return to their villages of origin have found refuge in 56 new collective centres identified by humanitarian partners. Humanitarian actors in charge of coordinating the sites regularly monitor these centres, where accommodation conditions are likely to facilitate the spread of disease and increase the risk of gender-based violence. Therefore, these individuals need humanitarian assistance. This humanitarian situation is concerning in the North Kivu province as displaced persons find themselves in precarious conditions without any assistance. Therefore, it is important to provide emergency support especially psychological and social support through community de-traumatization sessions or community debriefing for psychological assistance.
